# Timeline Studio: instructions for AI assistants

Timeline Studio (https://tl.gaup.uk/) turns a small plain-text format into one
of two kinds of page:

- a **day plan**: events at times of day, on dates (a day out, a trip, an
  agenda, a conference);
- a **routine**: steps someone follows live from a **Start** button (a
  workout, a recipe, a practice session, a cleaning routine). A routine has no
  clock times and no date; it runs from whenever they press Start, with a
  countdown, beeps and the steps announced aloud.

You are reading this because a person wants you to write one. Follow this
page: pick the kind, write the text, then give the person an "open" link and
the text itself.

If you have the Timeline Studio connector (tools named `create_timeline`,
`get_timeline`, `update_timeline`, `format_guide`), use it instead of building
a link: it checks the text, saves it and returns a short link to give the
person, and it can change the same timeline later. Its address is
https://tl.gaup.uk/mcp (no sign-in).

## Pick the kind first

If the person will do it step by step from a start moment (cook it, train it,
practise it, clean it), write a **routine**, even if they also say when
("dinner at 7", "my 6 AM workout"). A routine's first step starts with its
length, `+45s | Plank` or `+15m | Preheat the oven`, and it never contains
clock times (5:00 PM, 17:00) or a `date:`. If they named a time, say it in your
reply instead: "It takes 45 minutes: start by 6:15 for dinner at 7."

Anything that happens at times of day, possibly over several days, is a
**day plan** (see The format). Never mix the two in one text.

## What to send back

1. A link that opens the timeline, built like this:

       https://tl.gaup.uk/#text=<the whole timeline text, percent-encoded>

   Percent-encode the text the way JavaScript's `encodeURIComponent` does:
   newline is `%0A`, space is `%20`, `|` is `%7C`, `:` is `%3A`, `@` is `%40`,
   `#` is `%23`, `&` is `%26`, `+` is `%2B`, `%` is `%25`. Letters, digits and
   `- _ . ! ~ * ' ( )` stay as they are. Encode every newline; a raw line break
   breaks the link. Show it as a clickable Markdown link, for example
   `[Open the timeline](https://tl.gaup.uk/#text=title%3A%20...)`.

2. The same text in a ```text code block, so the person can paste it by hand:
   open https://tl.gaup.uk/, tap **✎ Edit** (bottom right), replace the text,
   tap **Done**.

If the text is longer than about 4,000 characters, skip the link and give only
the code block with the paste instructions. If you can run code, build the link
with `"https://tl.gaup.uk/#text=" + encodeURIComponent(text)` rather than by hand.

Opening the link loads the timeline without saving anything. The person's first
edit gives it a permanent address that follows later edits. The text in the
fragment never reaches a server until then.

To change an existing timeline, the person can paste its text to you; edit it
and send back the complete new text and link, keeping lines you did not need
to change exactly as they were.

## The format

Both kinds use this format; a routine differs only in its times (see
Routines below). A timeline is lines of text. Settings are `key: value` lines; events are lines
of fields separated by `|`. Lines starting with `#` are comments. Blank lines
are ignored.

    title: A Day in Los Angeles
    date: Saturday, Jun 6, 2026
    subtitle: Sunshine, tacos, and a sunset
    range: 08:00 - 20:00
    theme: travel
    city: Los Angeles
    timezone: PT

    08:00 | Coffee and pastries | Neighborhood bakery | coffee | sand
    09:30 | Griffith Observatory | Hike up, skip the parking | pin | sky
    11:30 | Farmers market | Tacos for lunch @ Grand Central Market | meal | sage
    13:00 | Getty Center | Gardens first, then the galleries @ | ticket | sand
    15:30 - 17:30 | Venice Boardwalk | Rent bikes to Santa Monica | road | sky
    18:00 | Pier at sunset | Ferris wheel @ Santa Monica Pier | palm | sand
    19:30 | Drive home | | car | sage

    note: Observatory parking fills by 10 AM
    note: Sunset is around 7 PM
    footer: Bring sunscreen

### Events

    time | title | description | icon | color | picture

Only `time` and `title` are required. Leave a field empty to skip it
(`19:30 | Drive home | | car`). Write `\|` for a literal pipe inside text.

Time forms:

- `08:00`, `14:30` (24-hour) or `8:00 AM`, `2:30 PM`. Always give minutes.
- A span: `15:00 - 17:00` or `3:00 - 5:00 PM` (the start borrows the end's
  AM/PM). Spans draw a bar from start to end. Use them for things with a real
  duration (a flight, a tour, a meeting).
- Start plus duration: `15:00 +2h`, `15:00 +90m`, `15:00 +1h30`.

Events are sorted by time, so list order does not matter; equal times keep
their written order. Keep titles short (2 to 5 words) and put detail in the
description.

Icons (pick one, or leave empty and the studio guesses from the words):
`home`, `plane`, `depart`, `land`, `coffee`, `meal`, `tree`, `bed`, `shop`,
`ticket`, `pin`, `car`, `road`, `palm`, and for routines `dumbbell`, `run`,
`stretch`, `timer`, `pot`.

Colors: `sky` (blue), `sand` (yellow), `sage` (green). Use them to group
kinds of events (for example travel = sky, food = sand, outdoors = sage), and
be consistent within one timeline.

### Places and links

End a description with ` @ ` and a place name and the card shows a map chip
that searches Google Maps for it: `Tacos for lunch @ Grand Central Market`. A
bare `@` at the end means the title itself is the place:
`Getty Center | Gardens first @`, or `Manhattan Beach | @`. The `@` needs a
space before it. Use real venue names; do not invent addresses. Set
`city: <city>` so short place names resolve in the right town.

URLs in a description or note are clickable. Google and Apple Maps links show
as a "Map" chip.

### Settings

| Setting | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `title:` | Heading of the sheet. Always set one. |
| `date:` | Display text under the title, e.g. `Saturday, Jun 6, 2026`. |
| `subtitle:` | One short tagline. |
| `range:` | Hour scale, whole hours within one day: `07:00 - 22:00`. Omit to fit the events. |
| `theme:` | `travel` (default, illustrated header), `minimal`, `retro`, `future`, `code`. |
| `note:` | Repeatable. Short reminders shown in a notes block. |
| `footer:` | One line at the bottom. |
| `city:` | Added to every map search. Global, or per day. |
| `timezone:` | `PT`, `ET`, `CET`, `IST`, or an IANA name like `Asia/Tokyo`. Global, or per day. Only affects calendar export. |
| `places: off` | Stops the studio auto-adding `@ place` to events. |
| `clock: relative` | Optional: marks a routine (a first `+duration` step already does). |
| `cover:` | An `https://` image URL shown above the title. |

### Several days

Start each day with `day: <label>`. Events, `range:`, `note:`, `city:` and
`timezone:` lines under it belong to that day. Settings before the first
`day:` are global. A one-day timeline needs no `day:` line.

    title: Long Weekend in Tokyo
    theme: travel
    timezone: Asia/Tokyo

    day: Saturday, Jun 6, 2026
    city: Tokyo
    range: 08:00 - 22:00
    09:00 - 10:30 | Tsukiji breakfast | Tamagoyaki and tuna @ Tsukiji Outer Market | meal | sand
    13:00 | Senso-ji | Go early, it gets packed @ | ticket | sage
    19:00 | Shibuya crossing | Dinner nearby | pin | sky
    note: Get a Suica card at the airport

    day: Sunday, Jun 7, 2026
    city: Hakone
    08:15 +1h30 | Train to Hakone | Romancecar from Shinjuku | road | sky
    12:00 | Lake Ashi cruise | @ | palm | sage
    16:00 | Onsen | Towels provided | bed | sand

Write day labels as real dates with weekday, month, day and year
(`Sunday, Jun 7, 2026`) whenever you know them: the masthead then shows the
date span and calendar export works. Undated labels (`Day 1`) are allowed.

### Step notes

Lines starting with `- ` directly under an event line are that event's notes
(form cues, ingredients for a step). The card folds them behind "2 notes".

    18:00 | Pier at sunset | Ferris wheel @ Santa Monica Pier | palm | sand
    - Bring a jacket
    - Cash for the arcade

## Routines: workouts and recipes

A routine is followed live from a **Start** button rather than laid out on a
day. Write the steps in order, each starting with its length. **Start the
first step with a `+duration`** (`+45s | Plank`, `+15m | Preheat the oven`):
that is what makes the text a routine. (`clock: relative` in the header does
the same and is optional.) The page then shows a ready card with the total
time, what you need and a Start button, the steps in lanes (steps that
overlap sit side by side), and while running a countdown with beeps and the
steps announced; on a saved link every device with the link open follows the
same run.

- `+45s | Plank` is a step that starts when the line above it (in the text)
  ends, or at 0:00 if it is the first. Durations take `s`, `m`, `h` and
  combinations: `+45s`, `+2m`, `+1m30s`, `+90s`, `+1h`. This is the usual
  form: write the steps in order, each with its length.
- `5:30` is a moment 5 min 30 s after Start (M:SS); `1:02:03` is H:MM:SS.
  Never use AM/PM, clock times or a `date:` in a routine.
- A step with a fixed start: `0:00 +10m` or `15:00 +25m` (also
  `0:00 - 15:00`). These may overlap, for parallel recipe tracks (the oven
  heats while you chop). Keep the very first step a bare `+duration`.
- `- ` lines directly under a step are its notes: form cues, or a recipe
  step's ingredients and details. They open while the step is running.
- `day: Warm-up` lines are section labels on one continuous clock, not dates.
  `date:`, `range:`, `timezone:` and `city:` are ignored.
- Write repeated steps out in full (there is no repeat block). Title rests
  `Rest` (they show as slim rows).
- Put the equipment or the shopping list in `note:` lines, comma separated:
  each item becomes a chip the person can tick off.
- Leave the icon empty: plank/squat → dumbbell, jog/warm-up → run,
  stretch/cool-down → stretch, rest → timer, boil/simmer → pot,
  chop/roast/bake → meal are guessed for you.

A workout:

    title: 7-min Core
    theme: future
    subtitle: No equipment, one mat

    day: Warm-up
    +1m  | Jog in place | Easy pace, loose shoulders | | sand

    day: Main set
    +45s | Plank | Elbows under shoulders | | sky
    - Hips level with shoulders
    - Breathe out slowly
    +15s | Rest | | | sage
    +45s | Side plank L | Stack your feet | | sky
    +15s | Rest | | | sage
    +45s | Side plank R | Stack your feet | | sky
    +15s | Rest | | | sage
    +45s | Dead bug | Low back pressed into the mat | | sky

    day: Cool-down
    +2m  | Stretch | Child's pose, then cobra | | sand

    note: A mat and a bottle of water

A recipe, with steps that overlap:

    title: Sheet-pan dinner
    theme: minimal

    +15m         | Preheat the oven | 220°C, rack in the middle | | sand
    0:00 +10m    | Chop | Onions and peppers in thick wedges | | sage
    - 2 red onions
    - 3 peppers
    +5m          | Season the tray | Oil, salt and paprika | | sage
    15:00 +25m   | Roast | Until the chicken is golden | | sand
    +5m          | Rest and plate | Spoon the juices over | | sky
    27:30        | Toss the vegetables | Leave the chicken where it is

    note: 8 chicken thighs, 2 red onions, 3 peppers
    note: Olive oil, salt, smoked paprika

### Pictures

A 6th field on any event line (in both clocks) is its picture, shown as a
thumbnail on the card and large while the step runs; `cover:` puts a photo
above the title:

    cover: https://example.com/kitchen.jpg
    +45s | Plank | Elbows under shoulders | | sky | https://example.com/plank.jpg

When you write a timeline, a picture must be an `https://` URL of an image
that really exists: one the person gave you, or one you are certain of. Never
invent an image URL; leave the field out instead. The person can add their
own photos in the studio (tap a card, then **Photo**).

## Rules for a good result

- Output only the format above: no Markdown, bold or bullets inside the
  timeline text.
- Every event line starts with a time; in a routine, with a length
  (`+45s`), and the first one always does. Do not write events without
  times; if the person gave none, choose sensible ones and say so.
- A routine has no clock times and no date. A day plan has no `+duration`
  steps without a start time.
- Ask for missing essentials only when you truly cannot guess (usually the
  date). Otherwise make reasonable choices and mention them in one line.
- Keep it to what fits on a phone: about 4 to 10 events a day (a routine may
  have 30 steps), titles short, descriptions under about 60 characters, a few
  notes at most.
- Resolve relative dates ("next Saturday") to real dates.
